feedback: Holding the iteration-2 geometry is the right call. Across iterations 0 to 8, every run ended off_track with max_error between 0.0604 and 0.0617 m. The changes that moved line loss were span (iteration 1, removed it on oval and slalom) and y = 0.06 (iteration 3, brought it back). Footprint 12 vs 16 mm (iterations 1 and 2), kp 2.6 to 4.4 (iterations 2, 4, 7), wheel_track 0.10 and 0.15 m (iterations 4 and 8), mass 0.6 kg (iteration 5), wheel_radius 0.04 m (iteration 7) and y 0.02 m (iteration 6) all left max_error at the same value. Iteration 3 changed y and ki together, so the ki effect is not separable. None of these levers has moved the excursion, so I do not expect further span, footprint, mass or track tests to help. The package this iteration changes only kd (0.05 to 0.15), since the excursion looks like a transient rather than a steering-gain or inertia limit. Read the result as follows. If max_error falls below about 0.058 m with line loss at zero, the damping lever is real, and you can hold the geometry while I tune gains further. If max_error stays at about 0.061 m, the excursion is not controlled by any tested lever, so do not propose further geometry changes on the same basis. In that case, propose only a change backed by a new hypothesis about the start-up condition, and say what evidence would confirm it.
requested_changes: Hold the iteration-2 geometry this iteration (16 mm sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg), since the excursion did not respond to any geometry change tested so far.

If max_error stays at about 0.061 m with kd 0.15, do not repeat span, footprint, mass, wheel_track, wheel_radius or y tests. Propose a geometry change only with a named start-up hypothesis and the measurement that would confirm it.
If line_loss_events return at any track, report which track shows it, so I can check whether the kd change or the geometry is responsible.
